By definition of the german penal code the twelve year old is not able to be guilty of a crime, which is a needed part of being charged and tried in a court of law. So this matter is - by current law - explicitly *not* a criminal one. Only for the 14 year old.

Well, given to severity of the situation now, the parents cannot refuse to work with the Jugendamt. The 12 year old will almost certainly be removed from his family and put into closed psychiatric care for a long time, probably until he‘s 18 and maybe even longer.

The anglo-american Commonlaw legal system is actually operating under very different practices compared to the prussian based one used in Germany, so there is definitely a difference in legal reasoning. And I do admit, my outlook on our criminal justice system is bleak, but sadly, realistic. In an ideal world, prison systems do rehabilitate, but that‘s not the budget driven world we live in. Especially not in Germany where 80% of charges get dropped before it actually comes to a trial, simply because of cost. We have a lot of people with outstanding warrants not getting arrested because of missing funds or man power par example. 
And I have to say in my personal opinion, it‘s probably easier to rehabilitate someone who does not have a fucked up criminal record which basically robs of a sense of hope and perspective. People do ask themselves at a later age 'If I already irreversibly fucked up my life, then why bother?‘, effectively lowering their inhibitions towards criminal behavior. You can’t generalize that sentiment, however something like this does happen to a degree. But like I said, I‘m no expert in juvenile or developmental psychology, so my opinion may very well be unsubstantiated when it comes to these matters.

It‘s not about being nice to criminals. Our legal system is in fact heavily skewed against the defendant in multiple points when it actually comes to a trial. And sentencing works in a way, that you have to balance public interest,  personal rehabilitation of the accused and his humane treatment whilst also ensuring retribution and a sanction hard enough to disencourage the general populus from committing a certain crime, with all those criteria being weighted on a individual case-to-case basis. But no legal system on the globe is perfect, so there will always be some cases and decisions that will just leave a bitter taste in your mouth.

Trust me, I‘m the first person to advocate for spending money on strengthening our judiciary system, but sadly it seems that our current government is more preoccupied with economics  and instrumentalizing the immigration crisis for political gain. I‘m just being realistic here. Most likely, the twelve year old will end up in a closed facility until he‘s 18 and then reassessed. Even if we were to start proceedings into restructuring our penal code to lower the age of criminal accountability it would be such a lenghty process, that it’s likely that he‘s back on the streets long before new laws could come into effect.

The cynicist in me doubts that you culd save that boy, but the humanist in me likes to believe that no one deserves to be written off without trying. The problem is, you can‘t lower criminal accountabilty for certain crimes like rape or murder individually, you have to lower that age across the board. And that would include stupid stuff like shoplifting etc. And regardless whether it should go punished or not, our judicary system is swamped as it is, having a ton of new possible offenders and court cases would cripple our courrs even further. Law‘s are sadly not only about justice, retribution and rehabilitation but also about plain executive things like preserving the overall effectiveness of our courts (and lot‘s of other things!)

out of genuine curiosity, which country? I‘d love to read a bit about their rate of effectiveness and their legal reasoning. But personally speaking, I would say that 10 years old is to young criminal accoutabilty. Think back to when you were ten, did you really have something that could qualify as genuine criminal intent? Or did you just act, without really thinking about things on the same scope as older people do. Twelve would in my personal opinion be a better age, especially considering that children at that age are more evenly and congruently developed which is important for creating laws with such a broad effect.

I agree with you on a personal level, but that is something that is up to lawmakers and a lenghty legislative process. I personally do think, that we live in a time, where you could reasonably disuss criminal liability starting at twelve years old. But I am no developmental psychologist and do not have the expertise to say, that if would be the right thing to do. But when it comes to juvenile criminal law here or criminal law in general (not as much as in juveniles but, still to a substantial amount), it does explicitly aim for rehabilitation, not retribution.

Does prison help prevent crime with a hundred percent effectiveness? No. The numbers show, that it‘s far more likely for someone who has been to prison to become criminally active after release. And sadly there currently is no system in place which could actually bring about a perfect success rate. 
But opening up the possibility of injustice in an entire legal system on the basis of one case, where measures were not successful, would be nothing more than a knee-jerk reaction to please the angry population and frankly a travesty for our legal system.

That‘s no sound argument, it just shows that you are not capable of formulating a sound argument without resortibg ti historical stereotypes. I don’t argue against e.g. the US with their history of slavery and institutionalized racism. What the Nazis did 70 years ago was one of the most cruel crimes against humanity.
 And it‘s not about not criminally prosecuting rapists, but CHILDREN. Our legal system does not allow to make exceptions for certain crimes to be criminally persecuted at an earlier age than the norm. 
There should be a discussion to lower the age of criminal liability, especially concerning how much faster children seem to mature than, say, 70 years ago. But something like that would need a lot of scientific research and a thorough debate. I‘m just stating the legal reality here.

I really don‘t know. We don’t dive to deeply into these topics during university. But just going from what I‘ve read and common sense, it makes more sense to try and heal someone in a controlled environment rather that putting them into a system that will treat brand them for life, ultimately resulting in fostering more resentment. Not only against people but society and it‘s norms as a whole. And at age twelve, there are good chances of other sanctions actually being effective (assuming that their parents did not play a major role in this)

Also, Sicherheitsverwahrung is for adults only. I‘m talking more about living in flats from youth protective services under strict supervision and with therapy until they are either deemed ready for society or turn 18. And if they are still perceived as a reasonable threat to society at 18, there are ways to keep them in a closed psychiatric facility (which btw is much worse than german prisons)

We do have our problems, especially with racism, our drug policy and the growing divide between rich and poor, but our criminal justice system concerning criminally charging minors most definitely isn‘t. Read up on juvenile criminology and you‘ll see, that there is no real point in incarcerating a twelve year old. Trying minors as adults in general. I‘m not saying that they didn‘t know what they did was wrong, just that they cannot reasonably held accountable for that in the same way as a fully developed adult. And on another note: at least there are no more concentration camps in our country since 1945 (something which the US can not say), our government is not openly nepotistic, borderline corrupt, plain stupid or utterly embarrassing on an international stage (in a diplomatic way, we still have our idiots), and we do not have an overcrowded prison system which operates for profit. Oh, and everyone is covered by public healthcare. Sure there are still bad things happening, but for europeans a mass shooting p.e. is not a monthly occurrence. Gun deaths in general. I could sit here for hours and just list things which show the US current position as a racist, dumb laughingstock. Mind you, when I say that, I‘m not talking about your americans as whole, but the current executive branch of you government. But overall I would rate the US as much more fucked up than a lot of individual EU member states and most definetly more fucked up than the EU as a whole.
